alex: noticed a perf/regression oddity on prod canary. Mixtral-8B requests with head_dim=48 are sometimes hitting SDPA kernel and producing garbled tokens. nvprof shows a spike in memory ops and occasional CUDA OOB warnings in logs. repro and small traces attached below.

alex: logs (sanitized):
```
E 2026-03-15T09:12:23Z runtime: kernel SDPA selected for model=mixtral-8b, head_dim=48, seq_len=1024
W 2026-03-15T09:12:23Z runtime: mask padding misalign detected: stride=192, expected align=256
E 2026-03-15T09:12:23Z runtime: flash/SDPA out-of-bounds read suspected, falling back to slowpath
```

jia: can you paste the exact config you used to repro? is this only on A100?

alex: quick repro (local container):
```
# run inside our inference image
python -m infra.bench_gen --model mixtral-8b \  --head-dim 48 --seq-len 1024 --batch 4 --kernel-profiling
```
Observed: flash/SDPA selected, then kernel fallback, then output token corruption ~5% of runs.

omar: I saw something similar last month for qwen variants where head_dim%16 != 0 triggered a mask-pad corner in our Triton wrapper. Triton kernels can assume warp-aligned strides; if mask logic indexes per-head without padding you get lane garbage.

omar: quick diag notes:
- flash/SDPA path assumes contiguous KV layout with head_stride % 128 == 0 on A100 for best perf.
- when head_dim=48, our packing yields head_stride=48*4=192 which isn't a 128/256 boundary for some kernels.
- the masking code we use does `if (idx < valid_len) load` but compiled kernel may vectorize/loading in 16-byte lanes causing partial loads.

sana: any CPU-side mitigation we can apply quickly? or should we force-flash off for those dims?

alex: forcing flash off (i.e., set kernel preference to SDPA-slow) fixes correctness but regresses latency ~1.4x. want a less-penalizing fallback heuristic.

omar: proposal: runtime should prefer fast kernel only if head_dim % 8 == 0 AND head_stride % 128 == 0 (or the kernel-provided alignment mask). Otherwise prefer the safe kernel or use a small pad + memcpy fastpath. Also add a canary that runs 1 request through flash and verifies outputs match reference before enabling for that model/version.

jia: agree. can we implement two quick changes:
1) runtime check: if head_dim % 8 != 0, mark kernel as "needs-safe" (fast path disabled)
2) batching heuristic: avoid cross-batch packing that would change head_stride alignment (i.e., avoid packing different sequence lengths into same batch)

alex: rough pseudocode for check: 
```
if (head_dim % kernel.vector_width != 0) {
  kernel.allow_fastpath = false;
  kernel.notes += "head_dim misalign";
}
```

omar: also add a tiny unit test to our kernel-selection harness that enumerates head_dim in {40,48,56,64} and asserts no fallback OOB warnings and output-consistency against a known-good reference (CPU emu or safe CUDA kernel).

sana: is this QP for Optimize? we should add to perf regression dashboard and alert if fastpath-fallback rate > 0.5% for a model-month.

ci-bot: build 2026-03-15T09:30:00Z: test/runtime-kernel-selection passed (w/ new head-dim unit tests).

omar: steps I will take: add the head_dim alignment check + canary run in runtime (PR later today). add unit test in kernel-harness. will run canary on A100 and RTX6000.

jia: I'll open an incident/perf ticket so product/infra are aware, include latency delta and correctness samples. label: perf/regression, kernel-selection, mixtral, qwen.

alex: I'll attach sample corrupted token outputs and a short perf table:
- flash (unsafe): p50=32ms, p95=120ms, correctness=95%
- safe fallback: p50=45ms, p95=215ms, correctness=100%

sana: ack. prioritize correctness first. after Omar's change we can run a canary on dedicated and flip fastpath selectively per-model. :thumbsup:

omar: one more note — Triton 2.7 had a masking bug we worked around before; make sure our submodule is on latest patched commit. I'll include that in the PR diff.

alex: thanks. please @jia @sana tag me when you schedule the canary so I can capture traces.

sana: will do. next steps tracked in the ticket.
